name: Amir Salarpour
tagline: Secure and trustworthy perception for autonomous systems.
intro: I work on secure and trustworthy perception for autonomous systems, with emphasis on adversarial machine learning, vision-language models, and efficient 3D vision.
bio: I am a Postdoctoral Research Associate in the School of Computing at Clemson University and a member of TigerSec Lab, where I work with Prof. Mert D. Pesé on the security, robustness, and trustworthiness of autonomous-vehicle perception systems.
My research spans adversarial sensing, physical-world and black-box attacks, vision-language models for autonomous driving, robust 3D point-cloud perception, and dependable multimodal reasoning.

Previously, I was a Visiting Researcher at Carnegie Mellon University’s CyLab in 2023 and an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Sirjan University of Technology from 2018 to 2022, where I also served as Department Chair.
